newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electrolux's slides in gloomy markets.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux's slides in gloomy markets.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux AB said on Tuesday weak markets in all its European businesses and negative currency effects were behind a 13 percent drop in profits for the first nine months of the year.
"The strength of the downturn for white goods in Europe surprised us. We had expected a stagnant market," group CEO Leif Johansson told reporters.
The group posted a 2.42 billion crown ($368 million) profit after financial items for the first three quarters of 1996, compared with 2.78 billion reported for the same period a year ago.
Sales for the period fell seven percent to 82.92 billion crowns, and Electrolux said currencies had been one of the main contributors to the fall.

"The stronger Swedish crown had an unfavourable effect on sales and income in connection with the translation of financial statements in foreign subsidiaries, and led to a decrease in balance sheet items," the company said in a statement.

The stronger Italian lira, an important income currency for the company, was also behind the fall, Ericsson said, estimating the total negative effect of currency movements at between 200 and 300 million crowns.

This was only partly offset by in improvement in financial items from a negative 1.10 billion crowns to a negative 897 million crowns, a boost Electrolux said was due to lower interest rates and a stronger crown.

Weak performance from the industrial products division -- which mainly consists of the Granges engineering unit -- were behind a 15 percent fall in operating income after depreciation to 3.32 billion crowns.
"Granges reported a substantial decline in operating income, mainly as a result of lower sales volumes for rolled products and recycling services, as well as lower metals prices," Electrolux said.
The industrial products business area posted an operating profit of 309 million grounds, less than half of the 661 million reported for the first nine months of last year.

The commercial appliances division, which includes the group's commercial kitchen and laundry areas, and outdoor appliances, whose leading brands include Flymo and Husqvarna, also suffered a fall in earnings.
However, the operating profit of Electrolux's flagship household appliances business area was largely unchanged on the same 1995 period at 1.73 billion crowns.
With the European market for white goods declining in volume for the period as a whole, it took a firm performance from the North American operation to save the day, Electrolux said.

"In geographical terms, operating income rose in North America, but declined in Europea. Improved income was reported in markets outside Europe and North America, despite large investments in new operations."
Looking ahead, Johansson said he expected a modest recovery in the fourth quarter, but analysts should not expect miracles.
"Ahead of the fourth quarter we estimate that low interest rates and the general climate will contibute to an upturn, although it will not be rapid during this quarter," he said.
Analysts said the nine-month performance was roughly in line with expectations, but there were several problems that would need to be overcome in the short term.

"Group numbers were as expected, but the household appliance business area was better than expected. Comments about a levelling out in demand in the United States are worrisome. They tried to increase prices by ended up losing market share," Peter Knox of UBS in London told Reuters.
Even so, a recovery in the United states would not be enough to save Electrolux's bottom line, Knox said.
"What we need to see is an improvement in European spending. And we don't just need to see volumes coming back, we need to see the product mix improving," he said. ($1=6.569 Swedish Crown)
